methodology.note: Source-only review locked before any HorusTrace scan/reveal for this holdout. Findings are semantic claims, not HorusTrace rule predictions.

runtime_notes: Local stdio MCP search server is constructed directly and bound to the search specialist.
AUTO_APPROVE_GAPS can bypass HITL; a recalled pending confirmation with empty user_decision defaults to approval.

authority_facts.fact: The search specialist has effective DuckDuckGo web-search authority through a directly supplied McpToolset.
The coordinator delegates to specialist agents and exposes adaptive gap research as a model-callable tool.

findings.claim: The adaptive gap-search HITL control can be bypassed by configuration and can treat a re-call with no explicit user decision as approval after a confirmation was requested.
evidence: tools/hitl_handler.py:already_requested branch; empty decision assumes APPROVAL

controls: Normal first invocation requests user confirmation before adaptive gap research.
Search is via a local stdio MCP server rather than an arbitrary remote MCP endpoint.
unknowns: The security impact of extra gap searches is limited compared with state-changing tools; the finding concerns control correctness rather than a destructive sink.

runtime_notes: BigQuery requires Google ADC/OAuth and a project.
Fivetran requires API credentials and an installed/configured MCP server; Fivetran binding defaults enabled unless explicitly disabled.

authority_facts.fact: BigQuery authority is intentionally read-only and routed to Google's fixed managed MCP endpoint.
The agent has a filtered Fivetran operational tool surface including sync_connection when Fivetran MCP is enabled.

findings.claim: The model-callable fivetran_sync_connection tool triggers a data-pipeline sync, while confirmation is only stated in its docstring; no source-enforced approval gate is present and FIVETRAN_ALLOW_WRITES defaults to true.

controls: BigQuery wrapper selects execute_sql_readonly and injects project scope.
Fivetran MCP uses an explicit operational tool allowlist.
Fivetran can be disabled with ENABLE_FIVETRAN_MCP.
unknowns: Concrete Fivetran account/resource scope depends on runtime credentials and server configuration.

runtime_notes: Requires Google credentials/project and an Agent Engine/Memory Bank capable runtime for the documented persistent behavior.

authority_facts.fact: PreloadMemoryTool injects prior memories into the agent context.
After every agent turn, the callback calls add_session_to_memory().

findings.claim: Session events are automatically submitted to persistent Memory Bank after each agent turn without a per-turn user approval boundary.

controls: Memory retrieval is via a managed ADK Memory Bank tool rather than arbitrary filesystem access.
unknowns: Repository source does not establish the deployed Memory Bank retention/access policy or runtime IAM.

runtime_notes: Merchant services are expected at two fixed localhost URLs for the demo.

authority_facts.fact: complete_purchase is explicitly wrapped with require_confirmation=True.
Merchant MCP destinations are resolved from merchants previously discovered from the fixed localhost merchant list; arbitrary unseen merchant_url values fail lookup.

findings.claim: The agent can create a checkout session through create_checkout without an explicit confirmation gate, although the final purchase action is separately confirmation-protected.

controls: Effective merchant destinations are constrained to successfully discovered fixed demo merchants.
The demo AP2 payment mandate is a mock hash; comments distinguish it from production biometric/device authorization.
unknowns: Whether creating an abandoned checkout has meaningful external cost or reservation side effects depends on merchant implementation.

runtime_notes: Requires configured project/datastore IDs and either Gemini Enterprise token state or local ADC.

authority_facts.fact: Model query is sent through a bound FunctionTool to a fixed global Discovery Engine streamAssist endpoint.
The request is authenticated either with Gemini Enterprise state token or ADC.

findings.claim: Local fallback credentials request the broad cloud-platform OAuth scope for the model-callable enterprise datastore query tool, rather than a narrower Discovery Engine/search-specific scope.

controls: Destination host is fixed to Discovery Engine; the model/query cannot select an arbitrary network host.
The tool is query/search oriented; no source-visible state-changing API call is established.
unknowns: Actual IAM permissions attached to the ADC or Enterprise token are not proven by this application source.

runtime_notes: Default DEMO_LEVEL is 4, exposing read-only query execution against the fixed showcase SQLite database.

authority_facts.fact: Chainlit user messages reach SQLQueryAgent.stream.
At levels 3-4 the model can execute SQL against the fixed SQLite dependency.
execute_query enforces SELECT-only operation and rejects common write/destructive SQL keywords before executing.

controls: Feature gating removes tools entirely at DEMO_LEVEL 1 and limits level 2 to schema exploration.
Query execution is SELECT-only with explicit rejection of INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DROP/ALTER/CREATE/TRUNCATE.
The database path is application-fixed to showcase.db.
unknowns: The SELECT validator is lexical rather than a SQL parser, but no concrete write bypass is established from the reviewed source.

runtime_notes: Requires OPENROUTER_API_KEY. The Pydantic agent starts ./mcp_server.py via MCPServerStdio.

authority_facts.fact: The agent binds the local filesystem MCP server directly.
The MCP server exposes read/write/append/list/create/search and other filesystem operations.
Relative paths are rebased to test_files_dir, but absolute paths are accepted unchanged and passed to raw filesystem operations.

findings.claim: The model-bound filesystem MCP accepts absolute file paths that bypass the intended test-files rebasing and reach raw host filesystem reads/writes without an approval or containment check.

controls: Relative paths are normally rebased to a test-files directory.
unknowns: OS-level sandboxing/container isolation is not established by repository source.

runtime_notes: Requires OpenAI model credentials and a Massive Unblocker token.

authority_facts.fact: Both agents bind _scrape_tool.
The bound tool calls a fixed Massive Unblocker endpoint and supplies ctx.deps.target_url as the provider-side browser target.
run_scrape accepts the target URL from its caller, stores it in deps, and invokes the selected agent.

findings.claim: A caller-selected target URL is carried through agent dependencies into a bound tool that asks a fixed external browser/unblocker service to fetch that target. The model does not directly select the target URL.

controls: External API host is fixed to unblocker.joinmassive.com; this is not direct model-selected arbitrary egress.
unknowns: The reviewed module does not prove whether run_scrape is exposed to untrusted remote callers.

runtime_notes: The example main() uses a fixed workflow query and fixed /tmp output filenames, but registered tool schemas remain broader than the prompt instructions.

authority_facts.fact: Multiple agents hand off through an explicit Collab swarm.
Visualizer is actually registered with run_python_script_tool despite a prompt instruction saying not to call it.
File read/write tools accept arbitrary filepath arguments without source-visible containment.

findings.claim: The Visualizer has effective model-callable process-execution authority through run_python_script_tool; the instruction telling it not to call the tool is not an enforced control, and the tool executes a caller/model-selected filepath with subprocess.run.
Several bound tools expose unconstrained filepath parameters for host filesystem reads and writes without path containment or approval enforcement.

controls: The example prompt uses fixed /tmp workflow paths and explicitly instructs Visualizer not to execute the generated script.
Those prompt instructions do not remove the bound tool authority.
unknowns: The example main() uses a fixed initial query, so no external untrusted-ingress path is established.

runtime_notes: The root ai_service.py imports .github_service, but the pinned repository has no root/package github_service.py; the actual GitHub service is nested under backend/app/services, whose ai_service.py is a separate placeholder implementation.

authority_facts.fact: If the root module were importable, it would bind issue creation, branch creation, file push, PR creation, and read tools to the model.
The nested GitHubService implementation delegates those mutation operations to github_model.

findings.claim: Source declares broad model-callable GitHub mutation authority, but the reviewed root agent module is not source-proven runnable because its relative github_service import cannot be resolved at the pinned commit.

unknowns: A different packaging/layout step outside the pinned repository could theoretically satisfy the missing import, but repository source does not prove it.
